title: Incident Response
description: Master incident response workflows, escalation paths, and communication patterns for production outages on Linux systems.

data.text: Incident response is the discipline of reacting quickly, safely, and transparently when production systems fail. A strong response process reduces mean time to recovery (MTTR) and keeps users informed even when things go wrong.
This lesson covers the structure of an incident response team, how to declare an incident, and what to communicate at every stage.
Every incident needs clear roles, even on a small team. Without defined responsibilities, well-meaning engineers duplicate work or miss critical steps.

items: Incident Commander: coordinates the response and makes decisions
Communications Lead: posts status updates to stakeholders
Technical Responder: investigates and fixes the issue
Scribe: documents timeline and decisions for the postmortem
Alert fires and page reaches on-call engineer
Incident Commander declares severity and opens incident channel
Technical Responder investigates using logs and metrics
Communications Lead sends initial status update
Mitigation is applied and system stabilizes

data.title: Declaring an incident via CLI
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Simple incident declaration script
# Usage: declare-incident.sh <severity> <service> <description>

SEVERITY=${1:-SEV3}
SERVICE=$2
DESCRIPTION=$3
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

cat <<EOF
Incident Declared
-----------------
Severity : $SEVERITY
Service  : $SERVICE
Time     : $TIMESTAMP
Summary  : $DESCRIPTION
EOF

data.title: Watch Out
data.text: Do not skip the status update step. Stakeholders who receive silence assume the worst. A simple message such as 'We are aware and investigating' reduces tickets and stress.

Escalation defines what happens when the on-call engineer cannot resolve the issue within a target time. A typical policy escalates to a senior engineer after 15 minutes and to management after 30 minutes.
Use consistent templates so responders spend time fixing, not formatting. Keep status updates short and repeatable.

data.title: Status update template
data.code:
Status Update - [SERVICE] [SEVERITY]

Current Status: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
Impact: Brief description of user impact
Next Update: [timeframe]

For questions, contact: @incident-commander

items: Define severity levels and escalation times in writing
Create status update templates before incidents happen
Ensure on-call engineers have VPN and production access at all times
Keep a war room channel pre-created for every service

data.title: Summary
data.text: Incident response is a team sport with defined roles and clear communication. Declare incidents early, communicate often, and follow an escalation policy. The goal is to restore service, assign accountability fairly, and learn from every event.
